summary: Former Forest Service fire lookout on Sherman Peak, Tulare County, documented 1923-1936; the summit now has radio transmitters and a public hiking trail.

facts.status_note: Forest Fire Lookout Association lists the tower as gone; SummitPost says only a few radio transmitters are on the summit today.
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Sequoia National Forest

access.note: A hiking trail climbs to the summit from Sherman Pass Vista. An old jeep road serves the people who maintain the radio towers.

visit.trail_note: About 5.2 miles round trip with close to 1,000 feet of gain. Sherman Pass Road is typically open late May or early June through mid to late November.

events.note: Fresno Bee reported that Jennie E. Abbott, the only woman the Forest Service employed as a lookout, would take up duties at the station on Mount Sherman on June 1.
George McComas, a Forest Service lookout, hurt his leg in May; in June a visitor spent two weeks at the Sherman Peak lookout station with Ranger McComas.
McComas came back in October after four months as fire lookout on Sherman peak.
McComas went back to Sherman peak for the summer in June 1936; a November 1936 item calls him a veteran fire lookout.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1923 item says Mount Sherman; the 1933 to 1936 items say Sherman Peak. The source page files them together, so the story treats them as one station. This is an assumption, not confirmed by a second source.

notes_for_editor: Not checked on the ground. Trail length differs: Wilderness Portal gives 5.2 miles round trip with close to 1,000 ft of gain (used in the story); SummitPost gives 5 miles round trip and about 700 ft. No build date found in any source, so the story starts at the first staffing item (1923). Last documented staffing is 1936; that is not an end date. Elevation differs: SummitPost 9,909 ft, Peakbagging 9918 ft; not used. The FFLA list gives no NHLR or FFLOS number for this site and the firetower.org and nhlr.org pages could not be reached, so no registration is claimed. The brief's agency field was generic; see corrections.
